title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.179): S is a scheme of characteristic p. f: X → S is proper and smooth of relative dimension n. X' = X^{(p/S)} is the Frobenius twist, with structure map g: X' → S, and F = F_{X/S}: X → X' is the relative Frobenius. E is locally free on X, Ẽ is its pullback to X', and F^*Ẽ = E^{(p)}.

The 'Frobenius' map (*) is Rf_*(Ẽ) → Rf_*(E^{(p)}). Its source is ≅ Rf_*(E)^{(p)} by base change. By Grothendieck–Serre duality, its transpose is the map Rf_*(Ě^{(p)}⊗Ω^n_{X/S}[n]) → Rg_*(Ě̃⊗Ω^n_{X'/S}[n]). This is induced by the duality trace of the finite flat morphism F, namely F_*Ω^n_{X/S} → Ω^n_{X'/S}, which is the Cartier operator.

This page draws the consequences.
(1) In top degree, the transpose of R^n f_*(Ẽ) → R^n f_*(E^{(p)}) is the map f_*(Ě^{(p)}⊗Ω^n) → g_*(Ě̃⊗Ω^n_{X'/S}) given by Cartier. The target is identified with (f_*(Ě⊗Ω^n))^{(p)} 'sous réserve de commutation à F_S', i.e. provided formation of f_* commutes with Frobenius base change.
(2) For E = O_X, the p-linear p-th power map R^n f_*(O_X)^{(p)} → R^n f_*(O_X) is the transpose of the relative Cartier operator C̃: f_*Ω^n_{X/S} → g_*Ω^n_{X'/S} ≅ (f_*Ω^n_{X/S})^{(p)}. This is the relative form of the classical Hasse–Witt / Cartier–Manin duality.
(3) The same holds for R^i f_*(O_X)^{(p)} → R^i f_*(O_X), provided the source is R^i g_*(O_{X'}). The dual map is R^{n-i}f_*(Ω^n) → R^{n-i}f_*(Ω^n)^{(p)}, obtained from C̃ by functoriality of R^{n-i}f_*.
(4) For i = 1 and f proper, R^1 f_*(O_{X'}) → R^1 f_*(O_X) is the map on sections of the vector bundles Lie Pic_{X'/S} → Lie Pic_{X/S}, using Pic_{X'/S} = (Pic_{X/S})^{(p/S)}. Grothendieck 'admits' that F^*: Pic_{X'/S} → Pic_{X/S} is the Verschiebung of Pic_{X/S}. He notes it is 'immediate' that F_Pic∘V = p and V∘F_Pic = p. A marginal note ('À vérifier') suggests this pullback gives a meaning to V for Pic under the general conditions he has in mind, where Pic need not be flat, so SGA3's V is not obviously available.
(5) The next page concludes that Lie(V) is the p-th power operation on R^1 f_*O_X, asking whether this is in Demazure–Gabriel, and that its transpose is Cartier on differential forms.

Purpose: a section of the Gauss–Manin / Cartier manuscript relating the Hasse–Witt operation, the Cartier operator and the Verschiebung of the Picard scheme via duality.
errors: The identification g_*(Ω^n_{X'/S}) ≅ (f_*Ω^n_{X/S})^{(p)} and the analogous ones for R^{n-i} need base change for Frobenius (e.g. local freeness / cohomological flatness). Grothendieck flags this himself ('sous réserve').
The notation f_*(Ω^n)^{⊗p} in the definition of C̃ should be read as the Frobenius base change ⊗_{O_S,F_S}O_S, i.e. ^{(p)}, not a p-fold tensor power.

That F_{X/S}^* on Pic is the Verschiebung is only admitted. It is correct for Pic^0 of abelian schemes / Jacobians (the dual of Frobenius is Verschiebung of the dual). The relation V∘F_Pic = p does follow immediately, since F_{X/S}^*(L^{(p)}) = F_X^*L = L^{⊗p}. For non-flat Pic, 'Verschiebung' needs a definition, which the note proposes to take as F^*.

ideas.what: The p-linear Frobenius on R^i f_*O_X is Grothendieck-dual to the relative Cartier operator on R^{n-i}f_*Ω^n, via the trace of relative Frobenius being Cartier
ideas.modern_name: Duality between Hasse–Witt and Cartier–Manin operators (relative version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957), Serre (1958), Manin (1963); relative versions in Katz (1970-72) and Mazur

ideas.what: The trace of finite flat relative Frobenius on top forms equals the Cartier operator
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator as Grothendieck trace for F_{X/S}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier; standard in duality theory (Hartshorne/Conrad, Illusie)

ideas.what: Pullback by relative Frobenius on the Picard scheme is the Verschiebung, and its Lie map is the Hasse–Witt map on R^1 f_*O_X
ideas.modern_name: Dual of Frobenius = Verschiebung; Lie(V) = Hasse–Witt
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda (1969), Mumford (Abelian Varieties), SGA3 VII_A for F,V

ideas.what: Using F_{X/S}^* to define a Verschiebung on a possibly non-flat Pic_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: Verschiebung of Picard functor via Frobenius pullback

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to take F_{X/S}^*: Pic_{X'/S} → Pic_{X/S} as the definition of the Verschiebung of a general, possibly non-flat or non-reduced, Picard scheme, satisfying F∘V = V∘F = p. This is left 'à vérifier'.
missed.quote: Je crois immédiat en tous cas que F_{Pic}V=p id, VF_{Pic}=p id ... À vérifier : cela y donne un sens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It gives a definition of V for non-smooth Picard schemes, relevant for non-reduced Pic in char p. But this is essentially folklore and appears implicitly in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the relative form of classical Hasse–Witt/Cartier duality and the 'dual of Frobenius is Verschiebung' fact. Both are well documented (Katz, Oda, Mumford). The only slightly novel touch is using Frobenius pullback to define V on general Pic.
transcription_corrections: 'M̄ comme pour les R^i f_*(O_X)^{(p)} → ...' should read 'Même [chose] pour ...'; M̄ is Grothendieck's abbreviation for 'Même'.

In the vertical isomorphism under the first display, the lower term is better read as (f_*(Ě⊗Ω^n_{X/S}))^{(p)}, i.e. the Frobenius base change of the f_* term. The marginal note 'car f_*(Ě⊗Ω^n_{X/S})' belongs to this identification.
'C̃ : f_*(Ω^n_{X/S}) → g_*(Ω^n_{X^{(p/S)}/S}) ≃ f_*(Ω^n_{X/S})^{(p)}'; the exponent is the Frobenius twist (written ⊗p), with 'sous réserve' underneath.
The final display reads 'Pic_{X^{(p/S)}/S} → Pic_{X/S}', with Pic_{X^{(p/S)}/S} ≅ Pic_{X/S}^{(p/S)} and the arrow labelled V.
